data.name: HttpsMissingTitle
data.value: The site does not answer over HTTPS

data.name: HttpsMissingRisk
data.value: Everything visitors read and type travels in clear: anyone on the same network can read it or change the page on the way.

data.name: HttpsMissingFix
data.value: Enable HTTPS with a certificate at your hosting provider (most offer a free Let's Encrypt one), then redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

data.name: HttpsUnusableTitle
data.value: The site could not be reached over HTTPS

data.name: HttpsUnusableRisk
data.value: If visitors cannot use HTTPS either, everything they read and type travels in clear. The connection did not fail because the port is closed (see the evidence): the server may be slow, or offer only a protocol this computer does not accept.

data.name: HttpsUnusableFix
data.value: Open the site with https:// in a browser. If it works, run the check again later; if it does not, enable HTTPS with a current certificate and protocol at your hosting provider.

data.name: CertificateNotRead
data.value: The certificate of the site could not be read.

data.name: HttpsBackToHttpTitle
data.value: The HTTPS site sends visitors back to HTTP

data.name: HttpsBackToHttpRisk
data.value: Visitors who ask for the protected site end up on the one in clear, where the page can be read and changed on the way.

data.name: HttpsBackToHttpFix
data.value: Remove the redirect from HTTPS to HTTP (web server configuration or site address in the CMS settings) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS instead.

data.name: HttpNoRedirectTitle
data.value: The site is also served over HTTP, without redirecting to HTTPS

data.name: HttpNoRedirectRisk
data.value: Visitors who arrive from an old link or type the address without https stay on the page in clear, which can be read and changed on the way.

data.name: HttpRedirectFix
data.value: Make the web server answer every HTTP request with a permanent redirect (301) to the same address in HTTPS, as the first step.

data.name: HttpClearHopTitle
data.value: The redirect to HTTPS goes through another address in clear

data.name: HttpClearHopRisk
data.value: Each step in clear is a point where a visitor can be sent to a false site before the protected connection starts.

data.name: CertNotYetValidTitle
data.value: Certificate not yet valid ({0})

data.name: CertExpiredTitle
data.value: Certificate expired ({0})

data.name: CertExpiredRisk
data.value: Browsers show a full-page warning instead of the site, and visitors who go on anyway can no longer tell the real site from a false one.

data.name: CertExpiringTitle
data.value: Certificate expiring in {1} days ({0})

data.name: CertExpiringRisk
data.value: When the certificate expires, browsers show a full-page warning instead of the site.

data.name: CertRenewFix
data.value: Renew the certificate and check that automatic renewal works (hosting panel, or the certbot/ACME job on the server).

data.name: CertIncompleteTitle
data.value: Incomplete certificate chain ({0})

data.name: CertIncompleteRisk
data.value: The server does not send the intermediate certificate of its authority: some browsers and many programs cannot verify the site and refuse it.

data.name: CertIncompleteFix
data.value: Install on the server the full chain given by the authority (the "fullchain" file), not the certificate alone. If the authority is a private one, this result is expected.

data.name: CertUntrustedTitle
data.value: Certificate not issued by a recognized authority ({0})

data.name: CertUntrustedRisk
data.value: Browsers show a full-page warning: visitors cannot tell the real site from a false one, and learn to ignore the warning.

data.name: CertUntrustedFix
data.value: Replace the certificate with one issued by a public authority (for example the free Let's Encrypt).

data.name: CertNameTitle
data.value: The certificate does not cover the name of the site ({0})

data.name: CertNameRisk
data.value: Browsers show a full-page warning, because the certificate belongs to another name: the visitor cannot know whose site it is.

data.name: CertNameFix
data.value: Issue a certificate that lists every name of the site, with and without www.

data.name: HstsMissingTitle
data.value: HSTS not enabled

data.name: HstsInvalidTitle
data.value: HSTS header not valid (no max-age)

data.name: HstsDisabledTitle
data.value: HSTS switched off (max-age=0)

data.name: HstsMissingRisk
data.value: Without HSTS the browser may still try the site in clear first; on an untrusted network that first request can be intercepted and the visitor kept on a false copy.

data.name: HstsFix
data.value: Send the header Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains on every HTTPS response, after checking that the whole site works over HTTPS.

data.name: HstsShortTitle
data.value: HSTS with a short duration (less than 6 months)

data.name: HstsShortRisk
data.value: The protection lapses for visitors who do not come back within that time, and they are exposed again on their next visit.

data.name: CspMissingTitle
data.value: No Content-Security-Policy

data.name: CspMissingRisk
data.value: If an attacker manages to insert a script in a page (a comment, a form field, a compromised plugin), the browser runs it with no limit.

data.name: CspMissingFix
data.value: Add a Content-Security-Policy header that lists where scripts may come from; start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only to see what it would block, then enforce it.

data.name: CspReportOnlyTitle
data.value: Content-Security-Policy in report-only mode

data.name: CspReportOnlyRisk
data.value: The policy only reports: nothing is blocked, so an inserted script still runs.

data.name: CspReportOnlyFix
data.value: When the reports are clean, send the same policy in the Content-Security-Policy header.

data.name: CspWeakTitle
data.value: Content-Security-Policy that does not limit scripts

data.name: CspWeakRisk
data.value: The policy allows inline scripts, eval or scripts from any site, so it does not stop a script inserted by an attacker.

data.name: CspWeakFix
data.value: Set script-src without 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval' and wildcards: list the sites you use, or use nonces with 'strict-dynamic'.

data.name: FrameMissingTitle
data.value: The site can be shown inside other sites (no clickjacking protection)

data.name: FrameMissingRisk
data.value: Another site can show yours in an invisible frame and make visitors click its buttons without knowing.

data.name: FrameFix
data.value: Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (or 'none'), and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN for old browsers.

data.name: FrameInvalidTitle
data.value: X-Frame-Options with a value browsers ignore

data.name: FrameInvalidRisk
data.value: Only DENY and SAMEORIGIN are honoured: with any other value the site can still be shown inside other sites.

data.name: NosniffMissingTitle
data.value: No X-Content-Type-Options

data.name: NosniffInvalidTitle
data.value: X-Content-Type-Options is not nosniff

data.name: NosniffRisk
data.value: The browser may guess the type of a file by its content, and run as a script a file uploaded as an image or a document.

data.name: NosniffFix
data.value: Send the header X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response.

data.name: ReferrerMissingTitle
data.value: No Referrer-Policy

data.name: ReferrerMissingRisk
data.value: What other sites learn about the page a visitor comes from is left to each browser's default; old browsers send the full address, which may contain personal data.

data.name: ReferrerFix
data.value: Send the header Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer).

data.name: ReferrerWeakTitle
data.value: Referrer-Policy that sends the full address to other sites

data.name: ReferrerWeakRisk
data.value: Every external site linked or loaded by the page receives the full address the visitor was on, including any personal data in it.

data.name: PermissionsMissingTitle
data.value: No Permissions-Policy

data.name: PermissionsMissingRisk
data.value: Third-party scripts and frames in the page can ask for camera, microphone or position as if they were the site itself.

data.name: PermissionsFix
data.value: Send a Permissions-Policy header that switches off what the site does not use, for example camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=().

data.name: CookieNoSecureTitle
data.value: Cookie without Secure ({0})

data.name: CookieNoSecureRisk
data.value: The browser also sends the cookie over connections in clear, where anyone on the same network can read it.

data.name: CookieNoSecureFix
data.value: Add the Secure attribute to the cookie (in the application, the CMS or the web server settings).

data.name: CookieNoHttpOnlyTitle
data.value: Cookie without HttpOnly ({0})

data.name: CookieNoHttpOnlyRisk
data.value: Any script in the page can read the cookie: a script inserted by an attacker can steal it, and with a session cookie take over the account.

data.name: CookieNoHttpOnlyFix
data.value: Add the HttpOnly attribute, unless the scripts of the site really need to read this cookie.

data.name: CookieSameSiteNoneTitle
data.value: Cookie with SameSite=None but without Secure ({0})

data.name: CookieSameSiteNoneRisk
data.value: The cookie is meant to be sent from other sites too, and travels in clear as well; current browsers reject it, so what depends on it may not work.

data.name: CookieSameSiteNoneFix
data.value: Add Secure, or use SameSite=Lax if the cookie is not needed from other sites.

data.name: CookieNoSameSiteTitle
data.value: Cookie without SameSite ({0})

data.name: CookieNoSameSiteRisk
data.value: Whether the cookie is sent with requests started by other sites depends on each browser's default; where it is sent, another site can act in the visitor's name.

data.name: CookieNoSameSiteFix
data.value: Add SameSite=Lax (or Strict) to the cookie.

data.name: SecurityTxtMissingTitle
data.value: No security.txt file

data.name: SecurityTxtMissingRisk
data.value: Whoever finds a security problem in the site does not know whom to tell, and the report may never reach you.

data.name: SecurityTxtMissingFix
data.value: Publish /.well-known/security.txt as plain text with at least Contact: mailto:<address> and Expires: <date within one year>.

data.name: SecurityTxtElsewhereTitle
data.value: security.txt redirects to another address, not followed

data.name: SecurityTxtElsewhereFix
data.value: Open the address in the evidence and check that the file has Contact and a future Expires; a redirect to another domain is allowed.

data.name: SecurityTxtNoContactTitle
data.value: security.txt without a contact

data.name: SecurityTxtNoContactRisk
data.value: The file exists but does not say whom to write to, so it is of no use to whoever wants to report a problem.

data.name: SecurityTxtNoContactFix
data.value: Add a line Contact: mailto:<address> (or the address of a web form).

data.name: SecurityTxtNoExpiresTitle
data.value: security.txt without a valid expiry date

data.name: SecurityTxtExpiredTitle
data.value: security.txt expired

data.name: SecurityTxtExpiresRisk
data.value: Without a current expiry date, whoever reads the file cannot trust that the contact is still the right one.

data.name: SecurityTxtExpiresFix
data.value: Set Expires to a date within one year, in the form 2027-12-31T23:59:59Z, and renew it before it passes.

data.name: DnsNameNotFound
data.value: the name {0} does not exist in the DNS

data.name: DnsNoAddress
data.value: the name {0} has no address in the DNS

data.name: DnsFailed
data.value: the DNS gave no address for {0}: {1}
